headline: OpenAI launches Presence for enterprise AI agents with voice and chat
summary: New platform aims to simplify deployment and management of reliable AI agents for customer-facing and internal business workflows.
details: OpenAI has announced Presence, a new enterprise product designed for deploying and managing AI agents across customer-facing and internal business workflows. The offering is available immediately through a limited general availability program, with deployments led by OpenAI Forward Deployed Engineers and select global systems integrators.

Presence is built to help eligible enterprise customers deploy agents that can answer questions, access company systems, take approved actions, and escalate to human workers, all while operating under company-defined policies and permissions. It aims to address the challenge of getting AI agents to behave reliably in production as business rules and customer needs evolve.

The platform packages the necessary policies, system connections, evaluations, guardrails, and update processes required to run agents within an enterprise. If businesses are looking to use AI agents but are unsure how to integrate OpenAI's models, APIs, internal systems, and security controls into a reliable system, Presence is designed to simplify that process.

The product is available today for real-time voice and chat experiences. OpenAI's announcement also describes broader ambitions for voice, chat, email, and other channels, though email support has not been confirmed for launch.

Presence integrates company knowledge, standard operating procedures, approved actions, simulations, evaluation tools, guardrails, and escalation rules. Customers can reuse some controls across deployments while customizing others for specific workflows or channels. Each deployment begins with a defined job, such as resolving a billing issue or handling an IT request, with the agent receiving only the necessary information and system access for that task.

Before deployment, agents can be tested against common requests, edge cases, and high-risk scenarios. Graders evaluate performance against intended outcomes, policy adherence, and proper escalation. Guardrails can intervene if interactions move outside defined boundaries. OpenAI has shared promotional screenshots illustrating simulation batches and performance monitoring.

The product continues to monitor performance post-launch, using production sessions, escalations, and quality signals to identify areas needing attention. Codex, with a Presence plugin, investigates these signals and proposes updates, which teams then test before a controlled rollout. This process aims to ensure agents remain reliable even as policies or user behavior change.

headline_marked: Samsung unveils Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Flip 8, starting at [[$1,199.99]]
headline: Samsung unveils Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Flip 8, starting at $1,199.99
summary: Samsung's latest foldable phones and smartwatches were announced at its July 2026 Unpacked event, with new models like the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Z Flip 8 launching August 7th.
details: Samsung has officially announced its new line of foldable phones and smartwatches at the July 2026 Unpacked event, with devices set to launch on August 7th. The new lineup includes the Galaxy Z Flip 8, Galaxy Z Fold 8, and Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, alongside updated Galaxy Watches.

The Galaxy Z Fold 8 introduces a new, shorter design with a 7.6-inch main screen and a 5.5-inch cover screen, starting at $1,899.99. It features a 50-megapixel main camera and a 4,800mAh battery, with configurations ranging from 256GB to 1TB of storage and up to 16GB of RAM.

The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra serves as a more direct successor to the previous generation, retaining the 8.0-inch main screen and 6.5-inch cover screen. It boasts a 200-megapixel main camera with 3X optical zoom and offers the same storage and memory options as the smaller Fold 8, priced at $2,099.99.

The Galaxy Z Flip 8, the most affordable of the foldables at $1,199.99, appears to have the fewest hardware changes. While its battery and camera specifications remain largely the same, it now features the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 processor, a notable upgrade from the Exynos 2500 in the Flip 7.

Preorders for the new Samsung Galaxy Z Fold and Flip 8 series come with incentives, including up to $350 in gift cards, and carriers like T-Mobile are offering significant discounts, with some deals knocking off up to $1,900 on select models.
